clue.text: Spotting little upper-class man hugging another one

indicators.note: hugging means pressed close against, so the second man sits right beside the first

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or upper-class man
another one means another man, and a servant is a man in the old sense of manservant

explanation.surface: Someone spots a little toff hugging another chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotting' looks like the act of seeing the hug, but 'Spotting little' together is the definition: noticing little.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who notices very little is inattentive, failing to see what is around them.

clue.text: Muses, say, why tennis can't be played?

definitions.meaning: the nine Muses of Greek myth make a group of nine, an example of the word
read as two words: tennis needs a net across the court

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why the Muses stop a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into NO NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine performers, and there were nine Muses.

clue.text: Director finally cutting our bit out — it's a wrap!

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A film director cuts our scene and calls the end of the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OUR BIT to BURITO; 'cutting' inserts R, the final letter from 'Director' picked by 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a tortilla wrapped round a filling, so it is a kind of wrap.

clue.text: Trainee flier's sub-par performance time

parts.note: in golf, an eagle is a hole played two strokes under par

explanation.surface: A trainee pilot's below-standard flight at a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub-par' sounds like poor, but in golf under par is good.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a bird still learning to fly.

clue.text: It is in estuary, outside of Rhode Island

indicators.note: outside of means without, so the state's letters are left off

parts.note: a river mouth is an estuary
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Something sits in a river estuary just outside the state of Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British bar, gin and it means gin mixed with Italian vermouth.

clue.text: Out to lunch, diner content to leave entree with less bread

indicators.note: out to lunch means crazy, so these letters go wild
the inner part, the content, departs, so only the outside letters stay

explanation.surface: A diner out for lunch is happy to skip the starter and have less bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content to leave entree' keeps EE, the outer letters, and 'Out to lunch' mixes them with DINER. Bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier means poorer, having less money, and bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Bad son's even seen entertaining King Lear production?

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the letters take the king inside them
bad means faulty, so these letters are put wrong and reordered

parts.note: R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A poor son has seen a staging of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges SON'S EVEN SEEN to NONSENSEVESE, and 'entertaining' puts R inside. Lear is Edward Lear, not the Shakespeare king.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear wrote limericks and comic poems such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Forgetting half of news, European journo is doomed

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving something out, so letters go from the word

parts.note: Finnish describes someone from Finland
read as half of N's: of the two N letters, one goes
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A European reporter who forgets half the news is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of news' is read as half of the N's: FINNISH has two, and one is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone finished is done for, with no hope left.

clue.text: Touring Italy, purchases inspiring bag

parts.note: I is the international code for Italy

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the word takes another inside it

parts.note: shopping means the things bought
to bag or land something is to catch or secure it

explanation.surface: Touring Italy, one buys things that include a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Island hopping is travelling around from island to island.

clue.text: One who has dispiriting experience, wasting day

indicators.note: wasting here means throwing away, so the day letter is discarded from the word

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: Someone goes through a gloomy experience and loses a day to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, the one holding it.

clue.text: Reagan is irritated about Democrat presenting the Bushes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the abbreviation
irritated means stirred up and agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: Ronald Reagan is annoyed at a Democrat speaking about the Bush presidents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges REAGAN IS to GARENIAS, and 'about' puts it around D. 'the Bushes' looks like the Bush family of presidents but means shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenias are flowering evergreen shrubs, so they are examples of bushes.

clue.text: Light scuffle — kick out in the middle of it

indicators.note: in the middle of places the dismissal word right within the scuffle word

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or scuffle
to fire someone is to kick them out of a job

explanation.surface: A brief scrap breaks out, and someone gets kicked out in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something is to ignite it, which is the phrase's meaning as a verb.

clue.text: Island with a gripping entertainment industry — this one?

definitions.text: Island with a gripping entertainment industry — this one?

indicators.note: gripping means holding tight, so the island and A clasp the industry word between them

parts.note: biz is informal for show business

explanation.surface: A question: which island has a thriving entertainment trade?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: Ibiza is a Spanish island famous for its nightclub scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza, a Balearic island, is renowned for clubbing, so it is an island with a big entertainment trade.

clue.text: Naval officer once in the hold for fighting

definitions.meaning: Horatio ... was the British admiral killed at Trafalgar in 1805
a wrestling hold applied from behind the opponent

explanation.surface: A former naval officer is detained in the ship's hold for brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like a ship's hold or a prison but is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral is the famous historical figure; the full nelson is a named wrestling grip.

clue.text: Turned up in disreputable cafe, so likely to be shamed

indicators.note: Turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone turned up in a seedy cafe, so they are likely to be embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Turned up' reads the letters from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose face is to lose respect, to be humiliated in public.

clue.text: Stiff stone having curves

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
arched means curved like an arch

explanation.surface: A rigid piece of stone that is nonetheless curved.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Starched fabric is stiffened, and figuratively a starched manner is stiff and formal.

clue.text: Intimate garments thus put on a Swede, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above, so the garments come before

parts.note: bras are underwear
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Underwear is thus dressed on a Swedish person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a person from Sweden but is the vegetable, a rutabaga.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the cabbage family, and the swede (rutabaga) is one of its vegetables.

clue.text: A flight attendant moving ecstasy to Asia, perhaps

indicators.note: moving says one letter is shifted to another place in the word

parts.note: a steward serves passengers on a plane
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cabin crew member smuggles ecstasy to Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' takes the E of A STEWARD to the front. The surface paints drug smuggling; 'moving' really shuffles a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards Asia from Europe is travelling east, so it is an example of that direction.

clue.text: Hopeful cop in decline

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the police word goes within the other word

parts.note: to wane is to decline
to cop or nab someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A hopeful policeman whose career is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a police officer but is the verb meaning catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is an aspiring person who hopes to become something.

clue.text: Only 75 per cent inclined to work in workspace

indicators.note: only three quarters of the eight-letter word is kept, the front six letters

parts.note: studious means devoted to study and hard work

explanation.surface: Someone only three-quarters keen to do their job in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only 75 per cent' keeps six of the eight letters of STUDIOUS, dropping US.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist or broadcaster works.

clue.text: Wanting one more pickled shrimp

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter for one is missing

parts.note: tiddly is slang for drunk or pickled, so tiddlier is more drunk
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone wants one more pickled shrimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled shrimp' wants to be read as one thing, but 'pickled' belongs with 'more' as drunker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a small fish, or informally a small person, as a shrimp is.

clue.text: Items on French loaves about to fill Yankees?

indicators.note: to fill means going inside, so the short word sits within the bets

parts.note: a Yankee is a type of combined bet on four selections
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Things placed on French bread are about to satisfy hungry Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf is slang for head, so items on French loaves are French hats; a Yankee is a bookmaker's multiple bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Berets are soft caps associated with France, worn on the head, the loaf.

clue.text: In Cervantes, the end is charming and delicate

parts.note: Cervantes wrote in Spanish, where el means the
fin is Spanish for end, continuing in Cervantes' language

explanation.surface: A literary judgement that the ending of a Cervantes novel is charming and delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Cervantes' sets both words in Spanish, the language of the author of Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes a small, dainty, attractive person, like a fairy.

clue.text: Prominent means to deter a career in transport?

definitions.text: Prominent means to deter a career in transport?

parts.words: Prominent means to deter a career in transport?
parts.note: a raised hump in the road, literally prominent, discourages careering, that is driving too fast

explanation.surface: An outstanding way to put someone off a job in the transport industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' reads as a job, but it is the verb to career, to rush along; 'Prominent' means sticking up.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic-calming ridge across a road makes drivers slow down.

clue.text: Uniform holy man spun showing taste

parts.note: Uniform is the NATO alphabet word for U

indicators.note: spun means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque

explanation.surface: A holy man in uniform twirls round to show his taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury flavour, one of the five basic tastes.

clue.text: Sailor from the East spies skinny partygoer

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
the CIA is the US spy agency
lite means low-fat or slimmed down, as in skinny coffee

explanation.surface: A sailor from Asia spots a thin party animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialite is a person prominent in fashionable society who attends many parties.

clue.text: Master's large pocket

definitions.note: read as master is: the verb with 's as a link

parts.note: to pocket money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's big pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master's' looks like a possessive noun but is the verb master followed by 's, meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to learn it thoroughly.

clue.text: Channel in same broadcast feature

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing feature

explanation.surface: A feature on the same TV channel is broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges IN SAME to MENAI. The Menai Strait separates Anglesey from mainland Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea channel, and this one divides Anglesey from north Wales.
